chunks: Abi (radhi Allahu 'anhu) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Salama the seller of al-Sabiriyyah from a man from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever repents in a year, Allah will forgive him.' Then he said, 'Indeed, a year is a long time.' Then he said: 'Whoever repents in a month, Allah will forgive him.' Then he said, 'Indeed, a month is a long time.' Then he said: 'Whoever repents in a day, Allah will forgive him.' Then he said, 'Indeed, a day is a long time.' Then he said: 'Whoever repents when his soul reaches his throat, Allah will forgive him.'
ai.seo_question: When is the latest time a person can repent and still be forgiven by Allah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this chain to highlight the progressive urgency of repentance, moving from the relative abundance of a year to the critical immediacy of the soul's ascent (ruh) at the moment of death. This progression underscores the Shia scholarly view that while divine mercy is vast, the window for sincere tawbah narrows as the soul approaches the throat, making the final breath the ultimate opportunity for salvation.
